name: YouTube Shorts Ideas for Beginners
blurb: 45 beginner-friendly Shorts ideas, each with what to film, a 2-second hook and a format
title: 45 YouTube Shorts Ideas for Beginners (With Hooks)
description: 45 YouTube Shorts ideas for beginners: what to film, the hook for the first 2 seconds and the format. One person, one phone, no budget needed.
h1: 45 YouTube Shorts Ideas for Beginners, Each With a Hook
answer: These are Shorts ideas for people starting out with one phone and no team. Each idea tells you what to film, what to show or say in the first two seconds, and which format suits it, so you can pick one and shoot it today.

items.t: The takeaway that was not yours
items.d: Film a delivery bag at your door, then a neighbour knocking to claim it. Hook: open on you mid-bite as the doorbell rings. Format: 2-person sketch, vertical.

items.t: Who gets the last slice
items.d: Three flatmates, one slice left, and everyone politely insists the others have it. Hook: a close-up of the single slice with three faces leaning in. Format: sketch.

items.t: First day at a new job
items.d: Play the new hire who misreads every office rule. Hook: you walking in and saying good morning to the printer. Format: POV sketch, you play every role.

items.t: Grandparent reviews a gadget
items.d: A grandparent or older relative gives an honest review of a phone feature or kitchen gadget. Hook: their first blunt verdict before you even explain it. Format: talking head.

items.t: A text from your future self
items.d: Your phone buzzes with advice from you, ten years older. Hook: the screen showing the message preview. Format: one-person sketch with on-screen text.

items.t: The five-second rule courtroom
items.d: Two people knock the last cookie to the floor and one invents new rules to claim it. Hook: the cookie hitting the floor in slow motion. Format: 2-person sketch, or play both sides yourself.

items.t: Things people say vs what they mean
items.d: Act out three polite phrases, then reveal the honest meaning with a caption. Hook: the first phrase with a fake smile frozen on screen. Format: sketch with on-screen text.

items.t: Your alarm clock has feelings
items.d: Give your alarm a voice that gets more offended every time you hit snooze. Hook: the first ring and a voice saying you promised. Format: voice-over sketch.

items.t: POV: the first hour of your morning
items.d: Show your real routine in eight quick clips with captions. Hook: the alarm screen showing an honest time. Format: POV, no talking needed.

items.t: Rate my desk setup out of ten
items.d: Pan across your desk and score each item. Hook: start on the messiest corner. Format: voice-over.

items.t: One thing I do every Sunday
items.d: Film the weekly habit that keeps your week on track, like meal planning or cleaning shoes. Hook: the finished result first, then rewind. Format: voice-over.

items.t: What I eat on a busy weekday
items.d: Three simple meals filmed in a few seconds each. Hook: the fastest one already plated. Format: no-face, hands only.

items.t: Tiny upgrades to a small room
items.d: Show one cheap change, like a lamp or a rearranged shelf, before and after. Hook: the before shot with a caption asking if it can be saved. Format: before and after.

items.t: A day as a student in 30 seconds
items.d: One clip per hour from waking to sleeping. Hook: the time stamped on the first clip. Format: POV vlog.

items.t: Things in my bag and why
items.d: Empty your bag and explain each item in one line. Hook: the oddest item held up to the lens first. Format: hands and voice-over.

items.t: Cleaning one drawer in real time
items.d: Speed up a messy drawer becoming tidy. Hook: opening the drawer to reveal the chaos. Format: no-face timelapse.

items.t: A phone camera setting most people skip
items.d: Show one setting, such as the grid or exposure lock, and a photo before and after. Hook: the bad photo first. Format: screen recording plus voice-over.

items.t: Fold a shirt in three seconds
items.d: Demonstrate a quick folding method, then do it again slowly. Hook: the finished fold at full speed. Format: hands only.

items.t: One word in another language
items.d: Teach a useful word, how to say it and when to use it. Hook: the word written large on screen. Format: talking head.

items.t: The easiest way to tie a tie or scarf
items.d: Show the knot step by step from above. Hook: the finished knot, then the question how. Format: hands only.

items.t: A study trick that helped me
items.d: Explain one method, like teaching the topic to an empty chair. Hook: you talking to the chair. Format: talking head.

items.t: Fix a common phone annoyance
items.d: Show how to turn off a setting that bothers you, like keyboard sounds. Hook: the annoying sound itself. Format: screen recording.

items.t: Explain a fact with kitchen objects
items.d: Use fruit or cups to show something like the size of planets. Hook: the first object placed on the table with a question. Format: hands and voice-over.

items.t: Draw one thing in five steps
items.d: Sketch a simple animal or object, step by step. Hook: the finished drawing. Format: overhead, no face.

items.t: I tried waking up an hour earlier for a week
items.d: Film one clip each morning and give an honest verdict on day seven. Hook: day seven's face first. Format: diary vlog.

items.t: Can I cook with only three ingredients
items.d: Pick three things from your kitchen and make something. Hook: the three items lined up. Format: hands only.

items.t: Guess the sound
items.d: Record five household sounds and let viewers guess before the reveal. Hook: the first sound over a black screen. Format: no-face.

items.t: One photo spot, five different looks
items.d: Shoot the same corner of your home five ways with light and angles. Hook: the most surprising result first. Format: photo slideshow with voice-over.

items.t: Paper plane that flies the farthest
items.d: Test three folding designs in a hallway and measure. Hook: the winner gliding past the camera. Format: experiment.

items.t: Rebuild a meal from a photo
items.d: Try to recreate a dish from a picture with what you have at home. Hook: the photo and your version side by side. Format: split screen.

items.t: Speed-read a page and test myself
items.d: Read one page in a minute, then answer three questions about it. Hook: the timer starting. Format: talking head.

items.t: The worst job interview I have had
items.d: Retell a short, harmless interview mishap, or act out a fictional one. Hook: the last thing the interviewer said. Format: talking head or sketch.

items.t: A kind thing a stranger did for me
items.d: Tell a short true story about a small kindness. Hook: the moment it happened, in one line. Format: talking head.

items.t: What I would tell myself at 15
items.d: Three pieces of advice, one per clip. Hook: a photo of you at that age, or a caption if you prefer. Format: talking head.

items.t: The lost item that came back
items.d: Tell how something you lost found its way home. Hook: the item on screen. Format: voice-over with photos.

items.t: An unpopular opinion about breakfast
items.d: Defend a harmless food opinion in thirty seconds. Hook: the opinion stated in the first line. Format: talking head.

items.t: The silliest thing I believed as a kid
items.d: Explain a funny childhood belief and when you found out the truth. Hook: the belief said with total seriousness. Format: talking head.

items.t: A tiny mystery in my building
items.d: Narrate a small everyday puzzle, like a plant that keeps moving. Hook: the plant in a new spot. Format: voice-over, no face.

items.t: How I filmed my last Short
items.d: Show your phone setup, lighting and props. Hook: the final shot, then pull back to reveal the mess behind it. Format: behind the scenes.

items.t: Day 1 of learning a skill
items.d: Start a series on a skill like juggling or sketching and post progress. Hook: your first clumsy attempt. Format: diary series.

items.t: Viewer picks what I do next
items.d: Offer three harmless options and film the one people choose. Hook: the three options on screen. Format: series.

items.t: Remake one shot from my first video
items.d: Reshoot your earliest clip and compare. Hook: the old clip with a caption about how bad it was. Format: split screen.

items.t: Reading old notes from school
items.d: Read funny lines from old notebooks. Hook: the notebook opening. Format: hands and voice-over.

items.t: A spooky story in one minute
items.d: Tell a short, creepy but not graphic story with the lights low. Hook: the last line of the story first, then rewind. Format: voice-over.

items.t: Answer a question from the comments
items.d: Reply to one viewer question with a quick, useful answer. Hook: the question shown on screen. Format: talking head or voice-over.

sections.h: How to pick and film one of these
body: Pick the idea you could shoot in the next hour with what is already around you. Write the hook line and the final beat before you press record, because the middle is easier once you know both ends.

ol: Choose one idea and write the first two seconds as a single shot or sentence.
Plan three to six shots on paper and keep the whole thing between 15 and 60 seconds.
Film vertically near a window or lamp, and record sound close to your mouth.
Cut every pause, add captions, and check it still makes sense with the sound off.
Post on a rhythm you can keep for a month, then look at which hooks held people and repeat that style.

body.note: If you use music, pick tracks from the platform's own library or ones you have the rights to.

ul: Show the ending first: the finished result, then rewind to how it happened.
Start mid-action: the doorbell, the drop, the reach for the last slice.
Say the bold claim in your first line, then prove it.
Ask a question the video answers: Can this tiny room be saved?
Put text on screen that names the viewer: If you always hit snooze...
Open on the strangest object or sound in the video.
Use a time stamp or countdown so viewers know it will be quick.

faq.q: Do I need to show my face to start?
faq.a: No. Many ideas here work with hands only, voice-over or screen recordings. Start with whatever feels comfortable and add face-to-camera videos later if you want.

faq.q: Can I use the linked scripts on my own channel?
faq.a: Yes. The scripts are original and licensed CC BY 4.0, so you can film them on any channel, including monetised ones, as long as you credit Script: cv.cm in the description.

faq.q: How long should a beginner's Short be?
faq.a: As short as the idea allows. Most of these fit in 15 to 45 seconds. Cut anything that does not move toward the payoff, then trim again.
